I bought it Sunday, and toward the end of the evening playing it the difficulty had ramped up a lot.

Oh, it's probably not everybody's cup of tea (but then, what game is?), but it just manages to scratch a certain itch that no other game does quite like it for me.

Difficulty certainly ramps up quickly, but one thing I've noticed is also that I tend to get kind of a tunnel vision with regards to my approaches. After a couple of missions that went well I tend to use the same tools and tactics over and over, to the point where they just cease working for some missions. Stepping away for a second and trying something completely different (weapon loadouts, equipment choices like shields, etc.) often works like a charm at that point.

I have been experimenting with shields. For the maps with long or open shooting lanes I like using a shield or smg to open the door then get outta the way, with a rifle posted back a little ways ready to shoot over their shoulder.

Flashbangs are hit and miss for me. Sometimes they are the best option for entire missions, sometimes useless. I haven't found a use for the stun type grenades, even when I land one right under an enemy it seems to do nothing.

Flashbangs are a bit tricky because their effect doesn't last too long and you basically need to make use of their effect essentially right as they go off, which is easy when you know exactly where your enemies are, but often useless when you throw them just for precaution and end up taking too long to move up. Stun grenades are more for flushing enemies out of cover and are most effective against enemies that are not yet engaging any of your officers, and therefore also pretty good when just thrown for precaution, rather than to deliberately lock down specific enemies that you know their exact position of (which FBs are great at). Also used them a lot in large outdoor areas. So FBs to lock down enemies in specific areas deliberately, stinger grenades to disperse enemies out of more general, larger areas.

Any advice on some interesting game types or rules? I had never heard of it before this weekend, so I'm happy to learn more about it.

Yeah, there are a few things. Definitely play with the recommended sets. Those tend to be really well balanced with a few interesting strategies you can employ in each one. Especially go back to them if you ever get burned on a random set game that flies out of control.

There are so many expansions, but my favorites are definitely Seaside and Prosperity. Seaside adds a bunch of cards that have effects across turns, so you can do a little bit longer term planning. And Prosperity adds high cost cards which are a ton of fun.

Also, when you start to accumulate more expansions, I usually either play entirely with one expansion, or mix two of them 50/50. I pretty much never go full random with all the expansions mixed together. Each expansion tends to play with a few core mechanics which require other cards from the same expansion to work properly. MIxing everything together often results in a selection of cards which have no synergy what so ever, defying all your efforts to strategize, and dragging the game way out.
